Introduces a self-consistency framework that uses diffusion-sampled reasoning trajectories and a reward model to score intermediate steps.
The framework stitches top-scoring steps across trajectories into a composite rationale, then recomputes the final answer, separating exploration from evaluation.
Applied to math and coding benchmarks, the method boosts accuracy up to 23.8% without training, especially on harder problems.
The paper introduces a method that uses diffusion language models to generate many short reasoning steps, then picks the best ones.
Each step is scored by a reward model, and the top steps from different runs are stitched together to form a new, stronger explanation.
The stitched explanation is used to recompute the final answer, boosting accuracy on math and coding tasks by up to 23.8% without extra training.

bullets: Agentic AI enables cloud workflows where autonomous agents reason, invoke tools, modify infra, deploy services, verify outcomes, adapt over long tasks.

Framework separates graph engineering (workflow progression & verification), loop engineering (diagnosis, repair, retry), and agent harness engineering (zero-trust execution via identity, policy, isolation).
Evaluation on Google Cloud shows validated code repos, controlled execution, evidence-gated progression, operational deployment, and bounded recovery.
Agentic AI lets autonomous agents manage cloud tasks, from planning to deployment, by reasoning about state and using authorized tools.
The framework splits work into graph engineering (workflow steps and checks), loop engineering (bounded fixes and retries), and agent harness (zero‑trust security).
Tested on Google Cloud, it shows complete code repos, safe execution, evidence‑based progress, and limited recovery within set limits.
Graph engineering defines long‑horizon workflow progression and verification‑dependent transitions, enabling machine‑checkable repository and deployment evidence.
Loop engineering supplies bounded diagnosis, repair, re‑planning, retry, and re‑verification, constraining failure recovery within explicit operational bounds and termination criteria.

Agent harness engineering enforces zero‑trust execution via identity, authorization, policy‑scoped capabilities, isolation, and runtime safeguards, validated on Google Cloud with evidence‑gated progression.
